filename: Bayesian Deep Learning for Convective Initiation Nowcasting Uncertainty Estimation.pdf
title: Bayesian Deep Learning for Convective Initiation Nowcasting Uncertainty Estimation
ml_methods: MOPED (Model Priors with Empirical Bayes using Deep neural network)
code_availability: Hyperparameter optimization tool mentioned: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7787022; specific model code repository not explicitly given in a dedicated code availability statement.
testbed_rationale: The task is nowcasting / observational classification of convective initiation from satellite imagery and radar, not climate/earth system model parameterization or physical emulation.
pain_points: Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) require optimizing more parameters and struggle to converge to optimal solutions compared to deterministic models.
BNNs trained with random priors showed degradation at longer lead times (30 and 60 minutes) without task-specific hyperparameter tuning.
Deep ensembles (initial-weights ensembles) showed poorer spatial generalization over clear-sky non-CI regions and anvil cloud regions without convective initiation.
Diurnal variability in performance: nocturnal convection (around midnight) remains challenging to predict.
extraction_notes: The dataset is based on Fan et al. (2024), covering June-July 2020 and June 2021 over the US Great Plains. Data availability statement directs to an NCAR GDEX DOI repository: https://doi.org/10.26208/6Y59-0R80.
